content.text: Now that I have a better understanding of the tables, I will calculate the total quantity sold for each product in 2021. I will filter sales data from `hardware_fact_sales_monthly` for the year 2021, group by `product_code`, and then sum the `sold_quantity`.

args.sql:
WITH sales_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        product_code,
        SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_quantity_sold
    FROM education_business.main.hardware_fact_sales_monthly
    WHERE CAST(SUBSTRING(date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2021
    GROUP BY product_code
)
SELECT
    p.division,
    p.product_code,
    s.total_quantity_sold
FROM sales_2021 s
JOIN education_business.main.hardware_dim_product p ON s.product_code = p.product_code
ORDER BY p.division, s.total_quantity_sold DESC;

content.text: I have the total sales per product for 2021. Now, I will rank products within each division by sales, select the top three, and then calculate the overall average sales quantity for those top products in a single query.

args.sql:
WITH sales_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        product_code,
        SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_quantity_sold
    FROM education_business.main.hardware_fact_sales_monthly
    WHERE CAST(SUBSTRING(date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2021
    GROUP BY product_code
),
ranked_sales AS (
    SELECT
        p.division,
        p.product_code,
        s.total_quantity_sold,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.division ORDER BY s.total_quantity_sold DESC) as rn
    FROM sales_2021 s
    JOIN education_business.main.hardware_dim_product p ON s.product_code = p.product_code
)
SELECT
    AVG(total_quantity_sold)
FROM ranked_sales
WHERE rn <= 3;
